title: Find high-value orders
summary: Write a SELECT with a filter, ordering, and explicit columns.

scenario.briefing: The data team wants orders of at least 5000 cents, highest first. Write one query that returns exactly the requested columns.

objectives.description: Filter orders at or above the threshold.
Check understanding through the remaining explanation and transfer evidence.

hints: SELECT chooses columns, FROM names the table, WHERE filters rows.
ORDER BY total_cents DESC puts the largest first.
SELECT id, total_cents FROM orders WHERE total_cents >= 5000 ORDER BY total_cents DESC;

misconceptions.description: Returning every column when only two are requested.
misconceptions.feedback: SELECT * returns extra columns. Name the two requested columns explicitly.

sections.title: A query is a precise question
sections.body: SELECT names the columns, FROM names the table, WHERE filters rows, and ORDER BY controls output order. The result shape is part of the question. Returning extra columns can break a caller that expects a fixed contract.

sections.title: Boundaries are explicit
sections.body: At least means greater than or equal. The database evaluates exactly what is written. SQLite is used here as a learning runtime; PostgreSQL behaves similarly for this basic query.

vocabulary.definition: The clause that chooses result columns.
The clause that sorts result rows.

steps.title: Query the high-value orders
steps.prompt: Edit query.sql. Return id and total_cents for orders with total_cents at least 5000, largest total first.

tests.description: The query returns the exact expected rows in order.

database.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE orders (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id TEXT NOT NULL, total_cents INTEGER NOT NULL, placed_at TEXT NOT NULL);

steps.title: Query clauses

statements.label: WHERE filters rows before they are returned.
ORDER BY DESC sorts larger values first.
SELECT * always matches a two-column contract.

steps.explanation: Explicit columns, filters, and ordering make a query's contract clear.

accessibility.summary: The SQL editor and result table are keyboard accessible. SQLite loads only for this mission.
accessibility.keyboardNotes: Ctrl+Enter runs the query. Result rows are a real table.
accessibility.screenReaderNotes: The result table announces column names and row count. The test compares rows and reports the first mismatch.
